authorityReview.evidence: The fixed SparkVault implementation converts the caller-selected ERC-20 asset amount through its exchange-rate path, validates receiver (not zero or vault), taker roles and deposit cap, then pulls the configured ERC-20 asset from msg.sender and mints shares. Arguments remain caller-selected; the platform adds no amount/recipient/owner/balance/feed gate. Protocol cap/role/state and separate asset approval may reject calls; no automatic approval/grant or native-ETH wrapping is implied. The dated role and shared implementation-version evidence does not establish current proxy/runtime identity, initialized asset value, funding, live liquidity, execution success, or financial safety.

The fixed SparkVault implementation converts caller-selected shares through its exchange-rate path, then checks receiver, taker roles and deposit cap, pulls the configured ERC-20 asset from msg.sender, and mints shares. Arguments remain caller-selected; the platform adds no amount/recipient/owner/balance/feed gate. Protocol cap/role/state and separate asset approval may reject calls; no automatic approval/grant or native-ETH wrapping is implied. The dated role and shared implementation-version evidence does not establish current proxy/runtime identity, initialized asset value, funding, live liquidity, execution success, or financial safety.

The fixed SparkVault implementation converts caller-selected assets, checks/burns selected owner shares and, when owner differs from msg.sender, checks and spends existing share allowance; it then pushes the configured ERC-20 asset to caller-selected receiver subject to liquidity. No platform amount, recipient/owner, balance or feed gate applies; protocol state, allowance and liquidity may reject. No automatic share approval or completion guarantee. The dated role and shared implementation-version evidence does not establish current proxy/runtime identity, initialized asset value, funding, live liquidity, execution success, or financial safety.
